item.title: Bijan Robinson vs. Kenneth Walker: NFL rushing leaders face off Sunday
item.description: The 3-6 Atlanta Falcons have been more bad than good this season, but don't blame Bijan Robinson. The fourth-year running back has more than done his part over the first nine weeks. Robinson currently leads the NFL with 880 rushing yards going into Week 10. Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker isn't far behind. The Super Bowl MVP trails Robinson by just eight yards (872) ahead of Sunday's showdown in Atlanta. Walker's numbers are arguably more impressive since he has played in one less game this season. The Chiefs offense has come back to life with Walker in the lineup, which has taken some pressure off of quarterback Patrick Mahomes. Walker has also made an impact in the passing game, recording 26 catches for 172 receiving yards and four touchdowns. Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs ranks third in the NFL with 847 yards, followed by Tampa Bay Buccaneers running back Bucky Irving (825 yards) and Buffalo Bills running back James Cook (814 yards). The Falcons and Chiefs will face off this Sunday at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Both defenses have been solid this season, but Atlanta has struggled to slow the ground game in recent weeks. From Weeks 1-4, the Falcons were the best in the NFL against the run. However, they've been the league's worst run defense over the last four weeks, according to ESPN's Field Yates. item.title: Former president of Athletics NI pleads guilty to child sex abuse charge
item.description: Gerry Carson will be sentenced for a number of offences in January 2027. [BBC] A former president of Athletics Northern Ireland has been put on the sex offenders register after pleading guilty to a child sex offence at Belfast Crown Court. Gerry Carson, 84, from Kingsway, Dunmurry in County Antrim, changed his plea on Thursday morning. Carson had previously pleaded not guilty to the charge of sexual touching of a child. At a previous hearing in October, Carson pleaded guilty to two charges of stalking. He will be sentenced in January 2027. The offences happened between 2022 and 2024. Another charge of causing a child to engage in sexual activity has been left on the books. That means it's not actively being proceeded with, but can be reactivated or pursued at a later date if required. Carson who was wearing a shirt, tie, jumper and jacket in the courtroom replied "guilty" when re-arraigned on Thursday morning. The court heard a trial will no longer be required and Carson's sentence would be determined in the new year. Given his plea at Belfast Crown Court, Carson was put on the sex offenders register with immediate effect. The judge told Carson it would be important for him to engage with both the Probation Board and his legal teams in the coming weeks. The court heard medical reports were being put together, looking at issues around geriatric medicine, cognitive function and a wider medical picture. He was released on continuing bail until sentencing. Carson was president of Athletics NI between 2019 and 2024. In a statement, they said their thoughts are with "the victims, their families and all those affected. "Safeguarding is an absolute priority for Athletics NI. We provide comprehensive support to clubs to help them provide a safe environment for everyone involved in athletics." Carson was also on the board of the Sports Council - which is now Sport NI from 2000-2007. He was vice-chair of the body from 2003-2007. A spokesperson from Sport NI told BBC News NI they are "not aware of any allegations relating to him while in his role as a board member." They added that "they would encourage anyone who has experienced abuse, or wishes to report abuse to speak to the PSNI."

item.title: NFL rumors: Commanders rejected multiple trade calls for 2024 2nd-round pick who’s out of rotation
item.description: NFL rumors: Commanders rejected multiple trade calls for 2024 2nd-round pick who’s out of rotation appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Washington Commanders received multiple trade inquiries about cornerback Mike Sainristil ahead of the November 2026 deadline but ultimately decided against moving the 2024 second-round selection. In spite of his declining role in the secondary, general manager Adam Peters was unwilling to part with him without receiving a quality draft pick in return , according to ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler. “The Commanders received multiple calls on corner Mike Sainristil, a 2024 second-rounder who’s out of the rotation in the Washington secondary. The Commanders were only parting with Sainristil for a quality pick, though.” Peters’ decision was surprising given the team’s 2-5-1 record and Sainristil’s diminishing involvement. The 26-year-old’s declining impact has contributed to his reduced playing time. After appearing on more than 80% of defensive snaps in each of the opening two weeks, during which he surrendered three touchdowns and allowed completions on nearly 78% of targets, Sainristil’s involvement dropped below 40% in Week 3. He subsequently gave up two additional touchdowns, pushing his completion percentage allowed to nearly 85%. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Sainristil played only 8% of defensive snaps against the Indianapolis Colts before seeing close to half the workload versus the New York Giants in Week 5. In that matchup, he conceded three receptions for 49 yards and a touchdown. His six touchdowns allowed in 2026 have already equaled his entire rookie-season total. The return of 2025 second-round pick Trey Amos, alongside the consistent contributions of free-agent additions Amik Robertson and Rasul Douglas, has further pushed Sainristil down the depth chart. He managed just one defensive snap across the two games immediately preceding the trade deadline. While his defensive opportunities have nearly disappeared, Sainristil remains involved on special teams, where he has drawn attention as a gunner on field goals and extra-point attempts. The Commanders also reportedly continues to appreciate his work ethic and standing within the locker room. Currently in the third year of his four-year rookie contract, the former Michigan standout now faces the challenge of earning another opportunity in Washington’s secondary. With Robertson, Amos and Douglas handling prominent defensive responsibilities, reclaiming a regular role will not be easy. The Commanders’ refusal to trade him indicates they are still willing to give Sainristil an opportunity to turn his situation around. item.title: Dan Hicks, NBC Sports voice for 34 years of memorable moments, dies at age 64
item.description: Johnny Miller and Dan Hicks Photo Credit: Rusty Jarrett/PGA TOUR Dan Hicks, the voice of many memorable NBC Sports events over the last 34 years, died Wednesday at age 64. "Dan Hicks was an extraordinary colleague, friend and person," NBC Sports' Rick Cordella, Sam Flood and Molly Solomon said in a statement. "In his 34 years at NBC Sports, he was an exceptional storyteller and caller of games and events who elevated some of the biggest moments in sports history. From Olympic swimming and skiing to Notre Dame football, numerous other high profile events and especially as the signature voice of our golf coverage for the last 26 years, Dan's blend of knowledge, style, enthusiasm and humor informed and entertained fans for decades. But far beyond his on-air excellence, Dan was a better person who welcomed teammates with a smile, a joke, or a word of encouragement, sometimes all three in the same sentence. Our heartfelt condolences and love to his wife Hannah and his daughters Hannah, Ellery and Riley." Hicks' wife, Hannah Storm, a longtime NBC Sports and then ESPN anchor, posted , "Our family is heartbroken by the sudden and unexpected passing of Dan following an acute illness. He was a devoted husband of over 30 years, loving father to our three daughters, and cherished friend to so many. His loss is immeasurable. Dan was truly one of a kind and, quite simply, the person everyone wanted to be around. When he walked into a room, he brought the energy, the laughter and the people together. He was endlessly kind, thoughtful and funny, and he made everyone feel like they mattered. Our three daughters and I are heartbroken. We are grateful for the love and support surrounding our family during this incredibly difficult time. There are simply no words to express how much he will be missed." Hicks, part of the NBC Sports team since 1992, became the lead golf voice in 2000, plus handled play-by-play at 15 Olympic Games, including a record eight in swimming and the last four in Alpine skiing. This fall was his seventh season as the Notre Dame football play-by-play voice. He also called NBA and NFL games and the French Open. Some of Hicks' memorable calls included Tiger Woods' putt to send the 2008 U.S. Open to a playoff ("Expect anything different?") and, two months later, all eight of Michael Phelps' gold medals at the Beijing Olympics. Hicks called all 28 of Phelps' Olympic medals from 2004 through 2016. Dan Hicks, longtime lead golf play-by-play announcer for NBC Sports, has died following an acute illness. He was 64. item.title: Cowboys Skip Deadline Splashes To Bet On Existing Talent
item.description: Robert Goddin-Imagn Images The Dallas Cowboys stayed quiet at the trade deadline. While other teams scrambled for last-minute upgrades, Dallas decided to trust the players already in the building. ESPN insider Adam Schefter noted that the organization never appeared close to making another major deal. “It never sounded like they got close to making any big deals,” Schefter said, adding that there was no real movement on a George Pickens trade. This approach puts the pressure squarely on the current squad to deliver results over the final eight games. Why The Roster Stays Put General Manager Jerry Jones and the front office clearly believe they have enough pieces to win. They already spent a 2028 second-round pick earlier in the season to add cornerback Joey Porter Jr. from the Pittsburgh Steelers. That move gave the secondary a physical presence without burning up all their draft capital. The team said the addition was an aggressive upgrade to the roster. “Rather than surrender more draft capital, the organization will give its existing players an opportunity to deliver,” the report states. In the last game on Sunday, Nov. 8, Prescott threw for 335 yards and two touchdowns against Indianapolis. CeeDee Lamb caught 10 passes for 195 yards, proving he can dominate when given the ball. Javonte Williams also ran for 101 yards and a score, showing the run game can keep defenses honest. However, the defense faces a much harder test in the next matchup. In his last four games, Quinnen Williams has recorded 10 tackles for loss and four sacks, marking a recent standout performance. The Challenge Looming Sunday San Francisco enters the stadium on Sunday, Nov. 15, with a 7-1 record and a six-game winning streak. They are not just a good team; they have beaten Dallas in their last four meetings, including two playoff games. The 49ers added Keenan Allen to their squad before the deadline for a 2027 sixth-round pick. His arrival adds another layer of difficulty for a Cowboys defense that needs to limit explosive plays. Dallas coach Brian Schottenheimer admitted that tight end Jake Ferguson and running back Tyler Goodson will miss multiple weeks due to knee injuries. “A lot of these guys, they play on adrenaline,” Schottenheimer said, highlighting the team’s resilience despite these setbacks, according to WJOX-FM . item.title: Seiya Suzuki Message to Cubs Fans Sounds Like a Goodbye
item.description: Aug 25, 2026; Phoenix, Arizona, USA; Chicago Cubs outfielder Seiya Suzuki against the Arizona Diamondbacks at Chase Field. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Augustus Oswald, Site Editor The Seiya Suzuki message to Cubs fans never says goodbye, but it reads like one. The right fielder thanked Chicago for five years and said he will share more when the time comes. That time is close: Suzuki has until 3 p.m. CT on Nov. 17 to accept or decline the Cubs’ $23.15 million qualifying offer, according to MLB.com. Seiya Suzuki Message to Cubs Fans Sounds Like a Goodbye Suzuki’s note, posted on Instagram , thanks fans for the ballpark, the teammates and the chance to wear a Cubs uniform. He also made a point of mentioning his family. “Thank you also for welcoming my family with so much kindness. My family has come to love Chicago just as much as I do.” That line is the one that leaves the door open. He didn’t say he is leaving, and he did not say he is staying. He said there are still many things ahead and that he will share more later, which could point to a new deal in Chicago or a new home somewhere else. Either way, the Suzuki message is written the way players write when they know the next chapter is not entirely in their hands. It also says something about how he sees the last five years. He talks about the ballpark, the fans, and the teammates, not the contract or the numbers, and that tone will stay with Cubs fans whatever he decides. The timing adds another layer. Nov. 17 is also the day Silver Slugger winners are announced, and Suzuki is one of three Cubs finalists . His defense also changed the conversation. After posting negative defensive numbers for much of his career, he finished with plus-5 outs above average, and he is a Gold Glove finalist. item.title: England's Mitchell could miss Six Nations after hamstring operation
item.description: Mitchell's four hamstring injuries this year have not all been on the same leg, with three to his right and one to his left [Getty Images] England scrum-half Alex Mitchell could miss next year's Six Nations after an operation to fix recurring hamstring issues. The 29-year-old, who was Steve Borthwick's first-choice nine last season, has gone under the knife after suffering four hamstring injuries this year. If Mitchell, who has recovered ahead of schedule in the past, follows an estimated four-month rehabilitation it would give him a chance of playing in England's final two matches, against Wales and Scotland on 6 and 13 March. Any setback however would leave him with only pre-tournament friendlies to play in for England before next year's Rugby World Cup in Australia. Mitchell's latest hamstring injury, which came in Northampton's win over Gloucester last month, ruled him out of this month's Nations Championship campaign. Mitchell suffered an injury to the same hamstring against Ireland in February and again against Fiji in July. He also tweaked his other hamstring - his left, non-kicking leg - in an England training camp in May. Mitchell told the i Paper last month that he had been given the option, like skipper Maro Itoje, to skip England's summer fixtures against South Africa, Fiji and Argentina, but opted to play instead. While Jack van Poortvliet has emerged as Borthwick's starting pick in Mitchell's absence, there is competition behind the Leicester man with Bristol's Harry Randall, Bath's Ben Spencer and Mitchell's club team-mate Archie McParland all vying for position. Mitchell travelled to Finland to be operated on by Lasse Lempainen, a specialist in elite sporting injuries. item.description: Dan Hicks , the soothing voice of The Players Championship through NBC's coverage for more than a quarter-century, died suddenly on Nov. 11 after "an acute illness," according to a statement released on social media by his wife, veteran TV sports announcer Hannah Storm. item.title: Ghana kick-start Afcon 2027 bid despite Ayew penalty miss
item.description: Jordan Ayew joined Championship side Sheffield United in September after spending two seasons with Leicester City [Getty Images] Ghana belatedly kick-started their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) qualifying campaign with a 2-0 home win over Somalia. The Black Stars had lost their opening two Group C matches against Ivory Coast and The Gambia, leading to the departure of coach Carlos Queiroz by mutual consent. Ghana women's coach Kim Bjorkegren was placed in interim charge for this month's double-header against the Ocean Stars, with the West Africans in danger of missing a second successive edition of the Afcon finals. The hosts were given a chance to take an early lead in Sekondi-Takoradi after Alidu Seidu was pulled down in the box, but Jordan Ayew's 14th-minute penalty was saved by Somalia goalkeeper Ibrahim Hussein. Ghana did go ahead in first-half stoppage time when Mohammed Salisu headed Mohammed Kudus's deep corner back across goal and Jonas Adjetey nodded in from six yards out. Felix Afena-Gyan doubled the Black Stars' advantage just after the hour mark when his shot from inside the box squirmed under Hussein and over the line. The result puts the four-time continental champions three points behind Ivory Coast and The Gambia, who meet in Bouake at 19:00 GMT. Cameroon, DR Congo and Senegal are also in action among seven other Afcon 2027 qualifiers on Thursday.

item.description: ‘This Was Forced on Them’ — Vikings Legend Cris Carter Explains Why Minnesota Had No Choice but To Reunite With Kirk Cousins The Minnesota Vikings brought Kirk Cousins back in a trade with the Las Vegas Raiders on Tuesday, less than 24 hours after Carson Wentz threw for 81 yards in a 23-6 home loss to the Buffalo Bills. Vikings Hall of Famer Cris Carter weighed in on the move and said, “There are a lot of people that are relieved.” The reunion is the latest turn in a quarterback search in which Minnesota has started eight different players at the position since Cousins tore his Achilles in October 2023. It also comes as the 6-2 Vikings look for answers on an offense that managed just 21 points across back-to-back losses. Cris Carter Ties Kirk Cousins Reunion to Struggling Minnesota Vikings Offense Carter shared his thoughts on the deal this week, first praising the Vikings’ defense and special teams unit, which have played at a high level, including kicker Will Reichard. His concern was the offense, and he viewed the move to bring back Cousins as a response to those struggles. “This was forced on them,” Carter said. He kept the mood light, however, while explaining who exactly is relieved: “Not only the Vikings fans … I was at the game with Randy Moss, Adrian Peterson, man, we’re glad because we thought we were gonna have to suit up because … with that Vikings offense, man, we could have helped them out.” The offense in question had just been held without a touchdown by Buffalo on Monday night. With Kyler Murray sidelined by a hamstring injury, Wentz completed 8 of 25 passes for 81 yards with two interceptions and a lost fumble before Max Brosmer came on late.
